title: Secularisation: Theories and Realities
welcome_lead: Are we really becoming less religious? Explore the secularisation thesis and its critics.
meta_desc: Religious Studies Adventure: secularisation thesis, Bruce, Wilson and contemporary trends.
final_note: You have weighed secularisation against the persistence of religion. The picture is regionally complex.

walkthroughs.body_html: Comte, Weber and Durkheim anticipated declining religious authority as societies modernised. Bryan Wilson and Steve Bruce trace declining church attendance, religious belief and social influence in much of Europe. Indicators include falling Anglican attendance, declining baptisms and growth of 'nones'.

Peter Berger, once a leading secularisation theorist, recanted: 'the world today is as furiously religious as it ever was'. Pentecostal growth in the Global South, Islamic revival, US religious vitality and 'spiritual but not religious' identification complicate the thesis.

Pew Research projects Muslims and Christians growing globally, with the unaffiliated rising in HICs. Surveys reveal differential secularisation between Europe and the US, and within Europe between Scandinavia and Mediterranean countries. Migration and digital media reshape religious landscapes.

mcqs.q: How did Hume define a miracle?
options: The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
A violation of the laws of nature by a particular volition of the Deity — and he argued evidence for such violations could never outweigh the uniform experience supporting the laws.
Hume defined a miracle as something amazing or unexpected.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of virtue ethics?
options: Virtue ethics is about following the Ten Commandments.
Virtue ethics tells you which specific actions are right and wrong.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
On character and habits — becoming the kind of person who acts well, aiming at eudaimonia (flourishing) through practising virtues that lie between extremes.

mcqs.q: What is distinctive about the ontological argument?
options: It tries to prove God's existence purely from the concept of God — a priori reasoning needing no empirical evidence about the world.
The ontological argument uses scientific evidence to prove God exists.
The ontological argument is the same as the cosmological argument.
Hume believed all miracles in the Bible really happened.
